overview: Villagers with lives of their own: they talk, they remember, they ask for real help, and sometimes they ask for something you ought to refuse.
Standing in a village is earned by being there and behaving, and is never shown to you as a number.

1.1.7: A server that crashes while starting shuts down instead of hanging, and no longer saves empty quest state over the world's.
1.1.6: Describes itself in one short line of what it adds.
1.1.5: Village chests are marked as their chunks reach a player instead of all at once on join, and breaking a block only says so when it was a village chest.

Finding the nearest village asks the world once per chunk every few seconds, measures a village without a structure once, and a bell-less village is found from its beds near whoever is asking; a world's villages no longer carry into the next one opened.

The day's village upkeep runs a second apart instead of all on one tick, a village nobody is near is no longer counted as emptied, and the daily cleanup keeps the presence history of players in other dimensions.
Winning a raid raises your standing once, not again every ten seconds while the village celebrates.
Putting things back into a village chest counts only for the player whose chest it is, and a single player client no longer reaches into the server to check.

Villagers' names, unspoken remarks and grief are let go once they can no longer matter, and letters a villager sends later wait on the server's clock and end with the world instead of keeping a closed one alive.
The cheap checks go first: no villager search for a misnamed quest nobody has, no dialogue lookups while nobody is talking, and plot and standing lookups allocate nothing.
A village whose centre moves while nobody is near it is measured again once someone is.
A village chest found gone on a join is unmarked for everyone still showing it, as a broken one is.
1.1.4: A demo to play in PvP Dimensions' onboarding.
1.1.3: Drop changelog notes for changes nothing in the game shows.
1.1.0: A villager opens with one thing, and the buttons answer that thing.
What they say is heard in conversation or read on paper, never in chat.
A theft can be owned, denied, or put right by returning the goods.
Your quest book is a button in the action menu, not an unbound key.
Giving up a quest asks you in the notice tray.
1.0.0: Dialogue that answers the time, the weather and what you have done.
Eight bands of reputation, kept per village.
Three commitments at a time, and quests worth going for.
Misnomer quests, where refusing is the right answer.
Some quests leave the village lit or flagged afterwards.
Plots can be granted to a player the village trusts.
A village's chests wear a nose at the clasp, so the rule shows before it is broken.
